summary.headline: Symbiotec Q2 FY27 consolidated revenue rose 43% YoY to INR280 crore, helped by INR53 crore DCV milestone income; EBITDA up 88% to INR94 crore.
summary.overview: Consolidated revenue for Q2 FY27 was INR280 crore, up 43% YoY, and H1 revenue grew 25%. Q2 included INR53 crore of milestone revenue from the US dual-chamber vial (DCV) injectable deal, with balance milestones expected in later quarters. Adjusted EBITDA was INR94 crore (after INR3 crore one-time IPO expense) versus INR50 crore a year earlier; PAT was INR52 crore, up 169%. Management signed a 10-year take-or-pay fermentation CDMO agreement with a European alternate-protein company and kept FY27 guidance of about 20% revenue growth and 25% EBITDA growth, with a plus or minus 5 percentage point range.

financial_highlights.metric: Consolidated EBITDA (Q2 FY27, adjusted for INR3 crore IPO expense)

segments.name: API (steroid and hormone, plus classical fermentation)
segments.commentary: Q2 revenue INR227 crore, up 16% YoY; H1 up 11%, driven mainly by volume and product/geography mix. Gross margin above 60%, EBITDA margin around 30%. Management guides high-single-digit growth with possible low-double-digit upside; about 70% of the business is regulated markets.

segments.name: Complex injectables (DCV platform)
segments.commentary: Long-term US agreement signed 30 Sep 2026 for 2 complex injectable products; INR53 crore milestone recognised in Q2 and balance to follow in later quarters. First ANDA filed Sep 2026, second planned in Q4 FY27; commercial product supply expected FY28, with profit share as a third revenue stream.

segments.name: Fermentation CDMO / biomanufacturing
segments.commentary: Ujjain site has 400 KL fermentation capacity. A 10-year take-or-pay contract with a US alt-protein company expects commercial batches in Q1 FY28. A new 10-year take-or-pay agreement with a European alt-protein company starts Phase 0 at the existing 100 KL scale, with Phase 1 (750 KL, up from 600 KL previously guided) taking 12-15 months to build.

segments.name: Biologics (insulin drug substance)
segments.commentary: Plant at 14 KL scale with capex just over INR100 crore; validation batches expected Q4 FY27, sales from mid FY28 after approvals, about 2 months later than earlier expectation. Around 50% of capacity committed to an Indian customer on a 5-year take-or-pay contract.

guidance_outlook: FY27 guidance maintained: approximately 20% revenue growth and around 25% EBITDA growth, with a plus or minus 5 percentage point range.
Milestone income from the DCV deal to continue across remaining FY27 quarters and at similar yearly intensity in FY28, though not linear quarter to quarter.

Fermentation: Phase 0 production at existing 100 KL from around end of FY27; Phase 1 commercial revenue mainly in FY29, with management saying FY29 would be the strongest year for toll fees of a few tens of millions of dollars.
Vegan vitamin D3: plant qualification by end FY27; sales to nutraceutical and veterinary markets from early FY28; pharma D3 may need another year. Pricing not yet decided.
Corporate capex to be kept at INR200-300 crore per year, with customers expected to fund a significant part of CDMO capex.
Management targets margins of at least 30% ROCE, 30-40% EBITDA margin and 70-80% gross margin across bio and pharma businesses.
capex_capacity: Ujjain fermentation site: 400 KL operational capacity today; 32 acres in possession plus about 40 acres recently acquired, for a 70-72 acre site.

European alt-protein deal: Phase 0 uses existing 100 KL, needing about 3 more months of fine-tuning; Phase 1 is 750 KL (up from 600 KL guided last quarter), with 12-15 months build; Phase 2 takes total to a few million litres. Estimated cost to reach Phase 2 about INR1,000 crore, largely customer-funded (undisclosed split).

Insulin drug substance plant (biologics, 14 KL): capex just over INR100 crore; validation batches in Q4 FY27; sales expected mid FY28 after regulatory approvals; about 50% of capacity committed to an Indian customer.
DCV: 20 million vial facility referenced by analyst; bag and syringe formats have proof of concept but no capex committed yet; capex decision expected in a quarter or two.
Vegan D3 plant under construction, qualification targeted by end FY27.
Over INR1,000 crore invested in the new business verticals to date.
demand_pricing: API price pressure continues across verticals; growth in Q2 attributed mainly to volume and product/geography mix. Management says steroid hormone growth remains high single digit.

Freight and solvent costs rose recently (Middle East conflict cited); management estimates a 2-3% hit to gross margin, seen as partly temporary, mitigated by backward integration and make-vs-buy choices.
Management says it has about 4 bio-manufacturing customers at advanced discussion stage, with traction also in the DCV space (3-4 more products in pipeline; talks with Europe and China partners).

Alt-protein CDMO: management cites the US customer's 10-year contract at about USD7-8 million per year, with inflation escalators; the European customer's toll fees are a few tens of millions of dollars at Phase 1.
Classical fermentation: 6-10 products in the pipeline, 2 commercialised for India; regulated-market entry 2-3 years away.
Premarin: API development done to FDA expectations; partner formulation in progress; launch likely years away with a generic already on market.

qa_highlights.question: Opportunity size of the European alt-protein deal and expected returns?
qa_highlights.answer: Management declined to give numbers. It is a 10-year take-or-pay with Phase 0 from 100 KL in FY27-end, Phase 1 (sub-million litres) in FY28 and Phase 2 above a million litres; toll fees start at a few tens of millions of dollars and could scale further. FY29 is expected to be the strongest year.

qa_highlights.question: Is DCV milestone income recurring?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said quarter-on-quarter intensity may vary but year-on-year it should be similar; milestones are expected to continue even after product sales start. Milestones are not linear quarter to quarter.

qa_highlights.question: Is the API growth from volume or price, and is the mix sustainable?
qa_highlights.answer: Growth mainly came from volume plus mix. Price pressure persists across verticals. About 70% of the business is regulated markets with sticky customers. High-single-digit growth guided, with possible low double digits.

qa_highlights.question: Why did the trade receivables rise from INR197 crore to INR268 crore?
qa_highlights.answer: Milestone invoices were raised on 30 Sep 2026 and collection falls in the next quarter, so receivables should normalise in Q3.

qa_highlights.question: Why did the CDMO capacity rise from 600 KL to 750 KL, and what is the capex and customer share?
qa_highlights.answer: The customer chose 750 KL instead of 600 KL and the agreement was revised. Management would not disclose the customer share, but said a significant part of capex will come from customers. Corporate capex stays at INR200-300 crore a year.

qa_highlights.question: Why has the insulin plant slipped and how much has been spent?
qa_highlights.answer: Capex just over INR100 crore. Revenue timing moved by a couple of months after a new biologics head changed plans for evolving regulatory standards. Only about 50% of capacity is committed to the Indian customer.

qa_highlights.question: DCV US approval timing?
qa_highlights.answer: ANDA accepted without refuse-to-receive (RTR); accelerated review granted; July goal date, but queries may delay approval. FDA inspection and ANDA approval are expected by late calendar 2027.

risks_watch: Milestone-driven DCV revenue depends on partner payments and ANDA timelines; second ANDA due Q4 FY27 and approvals expected late calendar 2027, with possible delays from queries.

Fermentation revenue is concentrated in a few alt-protein customers. Their scale-up and funding are unproven and they have a history of sector failures; the European partner's rival Liberation Industries term sheet was not clarified.
Insulin plant timing slipped by a couple of months; sales now expected mid FY28; only about 50% of capacity contracted.
API price pressure and rising freight and solvent costs (2-3% gross margin impact, per management).
Receivables spiked to INR268 crore at 30 Sep; watch Q3 collection.
Capex intensity: about INR1,000 crore for Phase 2 at Ujjain, with customer share undisclosed. Net debt of INR314 crore.
summary.management_tone: Confident and expansive on the fermentation CDMO and DCV opportunities, but evasive on quantified figures (customer names, capex split, deal sizes) citing confidentiality. Cautious on guidance, deliberately conservative on the API base business.
key_quotes: Of course, the reported revenues grew 43% year-on-year in Q2 FY27 and 25% in H1 of FY27, and reported EBITDA grew by 88% in Q2 and 29% in H1 of FY27.

This agreement offers three revenue streams for us, the development and regulatory milestones that we receive over a visible period of time, revenues from the product supply eventually, likely happening next fiscal year onwards, and share of profits on the partner sales product.

And of course, as our EBITDA improves, we will continue to plough back this operating surplus cash flow in our new capex because we see a lot of traction in biomanufacturing, including the biologics as well.
So we have technically only given around 50% of our capacities to this customer, though they can occupy 100% of the capacity.
We have a legally binding take-or-pay 10-year agreement on multi-million liter fermentation capacity with this customer for this product.

rows.label: Margin expansion
rows.why: Q2 EBITDA INR94 crore (adjusted) up 88% and API EBITDA margin steady at ~30%, but milestone income is one-time-like (INR53 crore of INR280 crore revenue) and management flags a 2-3% gross margin hit from freight and solvent costs.

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning
rows.why: Ujjain 400 KL today; Phase 0 at 100 KL from end FY27, Phase 1 to 750 KL in 12-15 months (approved), insulin plant 14 KL with validation in Q4 FY27, and vegan D3 plant qualification by end FY27.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: API guided high-single-digit growth with possible low-double-digit upside (H1 API +11%, Q2 +16%), plus US CDMO commercial batches in Q1 FY28 at about USD7-8 million per year.

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: DCV capex decision expected in a quarter or two for bag/syringe formats; corporate capex guided at INR200-300 crore every year and H1 capex already INR113 crore.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: FY27 guidance merely held at ~20% revenue and ~25% EBITDA growth (±5pp); API guided only high-single-digit, and management stayed conservative on the base business.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: Q2 growth was lifted by INR53 crore one-time milestone, API grew only 11% in H1, insulin sales slipped about 2 months to mid FY28, and freight/solvent costs cost 2-3% of gross margin.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: Second DCV ANDA in Q4 FY27 with commercial supply expected FY28, insulin validation batches Q4 FY27, vegan D3 sales from early FY28, and 3-4 more DCV products in pipeline.

rows.label: European alt-protein 10-year take-or-pay CDMO
rows.why: Signed 10-year take-or-pay; Phase 0 at 100 KL from around end FY27 and FY29 guided as strongest toll-fee year at a few tens of millions of dollars.

rows.label: Net debt pressure from capex
rows.why: Net debt INR314 crore at 30 Sep 2026 with H1 capex INR113 crore and Phase 2 Ujjain capex about INR1,000 crore, largely customer-funded (split undisclosed).

rows.label: Receivables normalisation in Q3
rows.why: Receivables rose to INR268 crore from INR197 crore on milestone invoices raised 30 Sep 2026, with collection expected in the next quarter.

tone.note: Management was confident on the fermentation CDMO and DCV opportunities but cautious on guidance and API base growth; analysts pushed on deal sizes, the European customer's funding and capex split, and whether the DCV milestones are recurring, which management would not quantify.
